title: Calculate Candidate Moves in 30s: Kotov Method Guide
subtitle: Stop aimlessly scanning the board. Master Alexander Kotov structured calculation tree for lightning-fast tactical vision.
excerpt: Stop wandering from move to move. Learn Alexander Kotov's structured calculation tree to spot checks, captures, and threats in under 30 seconds.
metaDescription: Learn how grandmasters calculate candidate moves fast using Alexander Kotov calculation tree method. Spot checks, captures, and threats in 30 seconds.
takeaways: Scanning C-C-T (Checks, Captures, Threats) filters candidate moves in under five seconds.
Kotov Tree Method: calculate each candidate branch deeply once rather than jumping erratically.
Look for loose, undefended pieces—every tactical combination begins with an unprotected target.
Disciplined calculation prevents time scrambles and eliminates careless blunder spirals.

content.text: In his landmark 1971 classic "Think Like a Grandmaster", Soviet grandmaster Alexander Kotov revealed the greatest weakness of amateur chess players: calculation wandering. A player looks at move A, jumps to move B, worries about move C, and plays move A with zero seconds left on the clock.
Step 1: Identify All Candidate Moves First

Before calculating a single variation, pause for five seconds and list 2 to 4 candidate moves. Look exclusively for forcing moves: Checks, Captures, and direct Threats (C-C-T). Forcing moves limit the opponent replies.
Step 2: The Kotov Tree of Analysis

Treat your calculation like a tree trunk with branches. Pick candidate move 1 and calculate to the end of the forcing sequence. Evaluate the resulting position. Then move to candidate move 2. Never return to move 1 unless you uncover an unexpected tactical flaw.
Tactics flow from a superior position. But spotting the tactic requires looking at the moves your intuition initially rejected.

items: Scan for LPDO: Loose Pieces Drop Off. Spot any undefended enemy piece on the board.
Check the King Geometry: Are enemy king and queen on the same diagonal (pin) or rank (skewer)?
Commit Decisively: Once you calculate a sound variation, play it with confidence—hesitation drains clocks.
